chapter: Going to New York and Capitol Records
title: Sent to Australia before the first album's release
summary: Levy sent her to Australia for three months, working the Chevron Hotel in Melbourne and Sydney.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Okay. We’ll start talking about albums in a minute. John had this notion, and he sent you out of the country.
So you go into the studio, record your album. Now the world is waiting for it to come out.
Um-hmm. But he did not want me to be in the States when it came out. So I went to Australia.
You ask John Levy that. I don’t have a clue.
Okay. He sent you to Australia.

I went to Australia, and we worked for three months. When I came back – it was the second album that Guess Who I Saw Today was in. When I came back, Guess Who I Saw Today had made its mark. I stayed in Australia for three months, I believe.
Chevron Hotel, yeah, both in Melbourne and Sidney.

Just that the little room in Melbourne we got, once my bags got in, I couldn’t get in. That’s all I remember about it. Then I actually moved out of the hotel into a bed and breakfast or whatever, something like that, because the hotel room was not working.
